still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market, and exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and Wegovy pill starting doses are still listed at $149 a month there, even though they are often waitlisted.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly are still the only sellers of branded incretins in the US, and Lilly still leads on efficacy.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in January 2026 is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the 503B compounding exclusion finalised from the April 2026 proposal still stands.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 25.0% ever-used minus 17.1% current leaves 7.9% of adults who have used the drugs and are off now. 44% of ever-users have cycled, which is 11.0 points: ~9.5 points are current users on at least their second course (~56% of current users) and ~1.5 points cycled and are off again, so ~6.4 points stopped once and never restarted. That is consistent with roughly one-third persistence at one year and 36–47% restarting within a year, compounded. 17.1% of ~268M adults is ~45.8M users. FICTIONAL payer mix (end-2030): Medicare ~12.2M (27%), made up of ~8.0M on legacy diabetes/CV/CKD/OSA codes, ~0.6M on the dementia-risk PA route and ~3.6M in the new obesity benefit (orals only, from Jan 2030); commercial ~12.8M (28%); Medicaid ~3.6M (8%); legitimate cash ~15.0M (33%); imported or counterfeit ~2.2M (5%, down from ~3M after India's export-licence rule). 12.2+12.8+3.6+15.0+2.2 = 45.8M. Age bands weighted by ~53M/89M/63M/61M adults give ~45.4M ≈ 17.1%. 65+ use of ~18.5% (~11.3M) is Medicare users minus ~1.4M disabled under-65 beneficiaries, plus ~0.5M 65+ on cash or retiree plans. Off-drug populations: ~0.7M cash users, mostly aged 18–35, stopped or dropped to sub-therapeutic doses after the Oct 2029 maintenance-price rise. ~0.8M former gray-market users lost their supply, and about half moved to TrumpRx starting doses they cannot titrate past. Adult obesity is ~33.9%. About 22% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, a group now concentrated in under-65 uninsured adults and Medicaid enrollees in non-covering states. Under-18 use fell from 0.8% to 0.7% after nine states restricted minors' prescribing. It is still concentrated in ages 12–17 in upper-income households, and some of those families now fill across state lines.

access.public_coverage: Medicare Part D obesity benefit (enacted Jul 2029 in the year-end health package, effective Jan 2030): oral incretins only (Wegovy pill, Foundayo), BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with a qualifying comorbidity, at a manufacturer-agreed $199/month net. The beneficiary pays $50 and Medicare pays $149. Arithmetic: ~3.6M enrolled by Dec 2030 × $149 × 12 ≈ $6.4B annualised. CBO scored the benefit at ~$58B over 2030–2039 net of modest offsets, about nine years at full run-rate with ramp. Novo's and Lilly's agreement to the $199 price was tied to a Section 232 pharmaceutical-tariff exemption for their US-sited fill-finish capacity. Legacy Part D codes and the dementia-risk PA route continue. Medicaid: 9 states still cover weight management at the $245 rate, and dual-eligibles have moved to the Medicare benefit. Medicare is now the single largest insurer of incretin fills.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is still $6–40/month domestically. Since India's Nov 2029 export-authorisation rule for small consignments to the US, delivered gray-market vials cost $80–180/month. Canadian generics are CAD 70–110. Generics are approved in ~170 countries, and India and China remain the world's volume source. Chinese generic tirzepatide is entering Gulf and Latin American markets ahead of patent expiry, where local law allows.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Price shock: oral semaglutide uses roughly 60–70× more API per patient than the weekly injection. Medicare's oral-only benefit landed on top of private oral demand, and Novo put Wegovy pill maintenance doses on allocation in Sep 2029. FDA listed semaglutide tablets 25 mg in shortage but not injectables. Compounders sued to compound under 503A and lost at district court in Mar 2030. TrumpRx prices: Wegovy pill $149 starting (frequently waitlisted) and $399 maintenance, up from $299. Foundayo $149–449. Injectables $349–499. Retatrutide (Zepbound-adjacent, BMI ≥35) cash ~$899. Lilly's small-molecule Foundayo absorbs most Medicare oral volume because it is cheaper to manufacture at scale. Orals are ~51% of all users and ~70% of new starts. Employer coverage for weight management is 41% (Business Group on Health 2030). Another 11% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks, now ~3.6M enrollees. Illinois and California (2029) ban adherence-conditioned premiums.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2029, BMI ≥35 or ≥30 with knee osteoarthritis-related obesity comorbidity under existing weight indication)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide, liraglutide; Wegovy pill 2028), now restricted by statute in nine states
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established cardiovascular disease (tirzepatide, Aug 2028; confirmatory trial enrolling)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs; oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 reads out 2031
dementia-prevention use by people without cardiovascular disease, cash-paid on orals and squeezed by the pill shortage
microdosing for 'steadiness', with use falling since the anhedonia label
nicotine, gambling and compulsive-shopping reduction: observational support only
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care, now barred outright in Utah and Tennessee
drugs.pipeline_note: No new indication arrived this step. The oral-parity driver was realised inside the rules as a new use of an existing product: in May 2029 FDA updated Foundayo's label with a switch-maintenance regimen after a 52-week trial in which patients induced on tirzepatide kept ~88% of their loss on orforglipron, against ~92% for those who stayed on injectable tirzepatide. In practice that removes the needle for maintenance at tirzepatide-level weights. No oral yet matches tirzepatide for induction. Retatrutide (BLA filed Feb 2027, under review at the start of the step) was approved Mar 2029 with a dysesthesia warning and BMI ≥35 labelling. Best efficacy is ~27% at 68–80 weeks, uptake is ~0.6M, and supply is limited. Survodutide (filed Jun 2028) received a complete response letter in Jul 2029 over manufacturing and GI-tolerability data and was resubmitted Apr 2030, with a decision no earlier than late 2030 and now expected Q1 2031, so Lilly and Novo remain the only US sellers. Amycretin was filed Jul 2029 and its PDUFA date moved to Jan 2031 after a major amendment. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 and not filed. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab-type) are in phase 3, with the first filing guided for 2031. Global incretin market ~$140B (2029). US volume is supply-constrained on oral semaglutide.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide's GI rates are highest at top doses. Forced switches between orals during the pill shortage produced a wave of re-escalation nausea.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; FDA switching guidance (Nov 2029) for allocation-driven substitutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; a small rise among new Medicare starts.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL settlement finalised 2029 without admission.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: An updated Medicare cohort (n≈3.4M) holds the 65+ hip-fracture HR at ~1.25–1.3 after 2+ years. Risk is attenuated (~1.1) among users with documented resistance training and adequate protein, a finding that tracks income. DXA uptake among 65+ users is ~38%. The 2030 wave of new Medicare starts is the largest unscanned older cohort yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained. The Medicare obesity benefit requires a baseline DXA within 12 months of start, which is widely unmet in rural counties. CMS DXA code continues.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflicting; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA adverse-reaction listing, no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the anhedonia analyses, which separate pleasure-blunting from mood disorder.

FICTIONAL: A pooled reanalysis of randomised trials with SHAPS data plus a 2029 randomised dose-reduction study found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6.1% of users vs ~2.9% on placebo, rising to ~8% at the highest doses. It is partly reversible within 8–12 weeks of dose reduction. Class labelling states the prevalence. Milder 'evenness' remains common and unmeasured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class labelling change (Mar 2030): Warnings and Precautions entry for anhedonia/emotional blunting with prevalence figures, advice to assess at titration and annually, and dose reduction as first response. A Medication Guide is required. EMA is evaluating.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Allocation-driven gaps in late 2029 produced measurable regain in ~0.5M cash users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; still underpins chronic-therapy framing and employer adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More case series in older new starts and low-dose self-managed users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Medicare benefit includes annual B12/vitamin D labs; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exists. The first interim pediatric bone-density data (2030) show slower BMD accrual in adolescents on drug vs matched peers, with wide confidence intervals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone postmarketing requirement continues; the interim data were cited in nine state restriction laws.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~8,900 cumulative FDA reports tied to non-approved product. The Indian export rule cut volume but raised the share of counterfeits sourced from unlicensed Chinese and domestic re-packagers. Mg/unit dosing errors remain the top poison-centre call type.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alert; CBP seizures; India's export-authorisation rule (Nov 2029) under the US–India trade framework; state marketplace suits.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reported in roughly 1 in 10 at top doses in trials, mostly mild; drives discontinuation.

food_and_beverage.state: About a third of households now include a user, and Medicare expansion added older households in Florida, Arizona and the Carolinas. Snack and confectionery volumes are ~7% below 2025 and sugary drinks ~7%. Dollar sales are roughly flat on price and premium protein lines. Senior nutrition (protein shakes, fortified soft foods) is the fastest-growing category after the Medicare DXA and protein counselling rules. Private-label protein is now a class marker in reverse: cheap whey in big tubs versus $4 single-serve 'clean' bars.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are ~10% below 2025 and beer ~6%. The decline slowed in 2030 as the anhedonia label cut microdosing, and some light drinkers came back. Mid-sized-city bar closures continue. Non-alcoholic and 'functional' drinks sold to on-drug drinkers are the growth line.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat, checks smaller. Retirement-corridor chains such as Cracker Barrel and Golden Corral face the Medicare effect: Golden Corral closed ~15% of Florida and Arizona units in 2030. Steakhouses and protein-forward fast-casual do well with high-income diners. Dessert attach rates are lower again.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are still contracting. Apparel has split along the class line: tailored, fitted 'lean-tier' athleisure at full price, and stretch, rental and resale for cyclers and regainers. Senior apparel had its own size-down rebuy in 2030.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans expanded resistance classes (SilverSneakers-type) because of the DXA and lean-mass rules. Boutique strength studios and DXA chains cluster in high-income zip codes, where a quarterly body-composition scan is a status routine.

insurance.state: Part D premiums rose ~6% for 2030, partly from the obesity benefit. Employer coverage fell to 41%, and some employers point retirees and pre-retirees toward Medicare. Metabolic tracks grew to ~3.6M enrollees and added anhedonia screening after the label. EEOC litigation risk is now in employer actuarial memos. Pharmacy trend is ~+8%.

pharma.state: Lilly and Novo dominate. Lilly gains share: Foundayo absorbs Medicare oral volume and retatrutide launched. Novo's oral API shortfall costs it a year of pill growth, and it is building peptide capacity in North Carolina and Kalundborg. Medicare's $199 net price is below commercial net but brings very large volume. Ex-US prices keep falling.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness alone no longer tells you much. A 70-year-old in Mesa can be thin on a $50 Medicare pill. What signals now is composition. Lean with visible muscle reads as money: trainer, protein, scans, the right drug at the right dose. Lean and soft reads as Medicare or a basic plan. A body regaining in patches reads as a cash user who hit the $399 maintenance price.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Class stratification has a uniform. In Plano and Frisco, Texas, corporate-campus professionals swap DXA lean-mass percentiles the way an earlier generation swapped marathon times, and fitted athleisure that shows the result is the dress code. Lower-income adults under 65 are the group the system skipped: too young for Medicare, too poor for $399, cut off by the mail-order squeeze. Upper-income teenagers in restricting states are taken across state lines for prescriptions; lower-income teens in the same states get none.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals stay shorter and smaller. Retirement communities like The Villages in Florida have reorganised social dining around small plates and protein. The Bread Alone fasting network claims ~550 congregations and has a sister movement in Black churches in Atlanta. Holiday tables are routinely planned for guests on different drugs and doses.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles have moved from 'on/off GLP-1' to body-composition flexes and, among the cash-poor, an explicit 'natural' tag. Since the anhedonia label, some people disclose dose as a courtesy. Desire mismatch remains a staple of couples therapy.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: The label has given the counter-movement a citation. 'Hungry' is a self-description on protest signs and in the Unmuted collective's posters. In management culture, appetite is still noise to be regulated.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Labelled since Mar 2030 at ~6.1% vs ~2.9% placebo, ~8% at top doses, partly reversible on dose reduction. Milder 'evenness' is far more common and unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Employers still say 'steadiness'. The FDA says 'anhedonia/emotional blunting', with a number. Clinicians now titrate to 'lowest effective steady dose'. Unmuted says 'sedation, now with a label'. Many users now have a name for something they had stopped noticing.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Metabolic tracks grew to ~3.6M enrollees, mostly in logistics, call centres, back-office finance and seven state employee plans. After the label, most vendors added a quarterly SHAPS-style questionnaire to the app. The stated purpose is safety. In practice it is another data stream, and some enrollees learn to answer it carefully. In Aug 2030 the EEOC issued a cause finding in one ADA charge, holding that a premium surcharge applied after discontinuation for a labelled adverse effect needs a reasonable alternative. Employers responded by offering dose reduction as the 'alternative' rather than dropping the tracks. Hiring managers still prefer 'steady'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Unmuted's 'off nights' have spread to Chicago and Oakland and are now a ticketed genre. Labels market 'unmuted' records. Sportsbook handle among identifiable users stays lower. 'Flat' fiction has a backlash genre about the first month off drug.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples now cite the Medication Guide in therapy. Planned drug holidays around anniversaries and holidays are common, and doctors increasingly sanction them as dose reductions rather than stops.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The left–right coalition widened after the label: MAHA-aligned legislators, labour, fat-acceptance groups, fasting congregations and now some psychiatrists. It won California's premium-conditioning ban in 2029 and a minors'-restriction wave in 2030, though the two halves disagree about which of these they wanted. A federal bill to repeal the 30% tri-agency wellness guidance has bipartisan sponsors and no floor time. There is still no measurable turnout or mood effect in elections.

state.regulatory_posture: Still fast on approvals (retatrutide, the Foundayo switch label) and now restrictive on use. In Mar 2030 the anhedonia class labelling came with a Medication Guide. A Jun 2030 FDA final rule ended the 'adequate provision' shortcut for broadcast drug ads, which effectively pulled incretin TV spots. Nine states limit minors' prescribing. Import enforcement leans on India's export controls more than on CBP.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Part D obesity benefit, orals only, at $199 net ($50 beneficiary / $149 Medicare), effective Jan 2030. The 30% tri-agency wellness guidance still stands federally. Illinois and California ban adherence-conditioned premiums.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM fill data, pill and pen logs, and now quarterly anhedonia questionnaires flow to wellness vendors under consent forms. Seven state employee plans cover weight GLP-1s only through monitored tracks. Two state Medicaid programmes still tie continued coverage to adherence and BMI progress. Medicare's benefit requires DXA and lab documentation but no adherence surveillance, which is now a talking point for both parties.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged (diabetes and cardiac codes only). The Army's supervised-oral recruit pilot was made permanent for applicants within 10% of standard but now screens for anhedonia at accession. DOT issued guidance (2030) that off-label alcohol-reduction use is not disqualifying for CDL holders, which trucking firms read as a green light.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs (2029) exempt US-sited fill-finish, which was the lever behind the $199 Medicare price. Under the US–India trade framework, India requires export authorisation for small semaglutide consignments to the US. Oral semaglutide API is the binding global constraint, and Danish politicians now argue over whether Medicare's demand is crowding out European supply.

events.event: FDA updates Foundayo label with tirzepatide-to-pill switch regimen after 52-week trial shows patients keep ~88% of injectable-induced loss; orals pass half of all US users by 2030
Year-end health package creates first Medicare Part D obesity benefit, orals only, at $199 net after Novo and Lilly win Section 232 tariff exemptions; CBO scores ~$58B over ten years

Novo puts Wegovy pill maintenance doses on allocation as API runs short; FDA lists tablets in shortage; TrumpRx maintenance price rises $299 to $399, weeks before India's export-licence rule lifts mail-order vial prices
FDA orders class warning for anhedonia/emotional blunting on all incretins, citing ~6% vs ~3% on placebo, and requires a Medication Guide
FDA final rule effectively ends incretin TV ads; by summer nine states, led by Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma, restrict weight-loss incretin prescribing to minors
EEOC issues first cause finding against a logistics firm's metabolic-track surcharge; employers respond by offering dose reduction as the 'reasonable alternative' and adding mood screening

open_tensions: Medicare is now the largest insurer of incretin fills through an oral-only benefit, just as oral semaglutide is the most supply-constrained product in the class. That leaves allocation between $50-copay seniors and $399 cash users unresolved, and the 2030 wave of older starts is the least DXA-scanned cohort yet.

The anhedonia label and the EEOC cause finding collide with the 30% wellness guidance. Employers kept the tracks by offering dose reduction and adding mood questionnaires, which turns a safety warning into another monitored data stream.

Body composition is now the class marker. Thin is covered for over-65s, while muscle-preserving adjuncts won't be filed until 2031 and lower-income adults under 65 sit between the price shock, the mail-order squeeze and no public coverage.
State limits on minors push upper-income families across state lines while the interim pediatric bone data stay ambiguous, so restriction is sorting adolescent use by income without stopping it.

prose.headline: Thin Is Covered Now. Muscle Is What You Pay For.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about seventeen American adults in a hundred take an incretin drug, a little more than two years ago. One in four has tried one. The headline number barely moved, but who pays and who looks how moved a lot.

The biggest change is that Medicare now pays. Last summer Congress did what it had refused to do when the Bridge pilot lapsed. It created a Part D obesity benefit, narrowed to make the arithmetic work: pills only, at $199 a month, with the beneficiary paying fifty dollars. Novo and Lilly accepted the price in exchange for exemptions from the new pharmaceutical tariffs on their American plants. By December about three and a half million older Americans had enrolled. Medicare is now the largest insurer of these drugs in the country, and in retirement towns from Mesa to The Villages, thin is simply what seventy looks like.

The benefit arrived just as the pills ran short. Oral semaglutide needs dozens of times more active ingredient than the weekly shot. When Medicare demand landed on top of private demand, Novo put maintenance doses on allocation and the FDA listed the tablets in shortage. The government cash channel still advertises $149 starting doses, which are often waitlisted. The maintenance price went from $299 to $399. Weeks later India, under its trade framework with Washington, began requiring export licences for the small parcels that had supplied three million Americans. Mail-order vials doubled in price. Some of those buyers moved to legitimate starting doses they can't afford to raise, and some stopped and are regaining. Lilly's small-molecule pill, cheaper to make, absorbed much of the demand. A label update now lets people who lost weight on its injectable switch to the pill and keep most of the loss, so the needle is gone even at the high end.

The second change is a sentence on every label. In March the FDA added a class warning for anhedonia: about six in a hundred users lose a clinically meaningful amount of pleasure, against three on placebo, and more at the highest doses. Clinicians now titrate to the lowest steady dose. The employers who built 'metabolic tracks' around steadiness, mostly logistics firms, call centres and seven state plans, did not drop them. They added a quarterly mood questionnaire to the adherence app and offered dose reduction as the reasonable alternative the EEOC now says they owe. Enrolment kept growing. Illinois and California still forbid tying premiums to adherence, and most states don't.

The states found something else to restrict. Nine, led by Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma, now limit weight-loss prescribing to minors, citing interim bone data that are suggestive and statistically thin. A federal rule took the drugs off television. Families with means drive teenagers to clinics in neighbouring states, and families without means don't.

Because thinness is common now, it has stopped signalling much, and muscle has taken its place. In the corporate suburbs north of Dallas, a quarterly DXA scan and a lean-mass percentile are status details, and fitted athleisure is the dress code. A soft, lean body reads as Medicare or a basic plan. Patchy regain reads as someone who ran into the $399 price. Drugs to protect muscle are still in trials. Until they arrive, holding on to muscle takes trainers, protein and time, and those cost money.

The industries keep adapting. Snack volumes are down, spirits are down further, and buffet chains in Florida are closing stores. The gyms that swapped treadmills for squat racks are now running Medicare resistance classes. The counter-movement is bigger, and it now has a citation for its slogans. From the outside, the country is thinner, older people are better covered, and things are calm. That is mostly true.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marcus Bell wakes at 4:40 in Southaven, Mississippi, and takes the white Foundayo tablet with water before his phone has finished loading. The app logs the time and asks him to confirm. He confirms.

At the freight yard outside Memphis he dispatches forty-one trucks. The radio chatter bothers him less than it used to. His supervisor calls him unflappable in reviews, and the word is on the form.

At ten the app shows a new screen: eight questions, quarterly, "for your safety." It asks whether he still enjoys the things he used to enjoy. He thinks about his daughter's softball, about barbecue, about the fishing trip he keeps postponing. He picks "somewhat agree" for most. He has heard that "disagree" triggers a call from a nurse about lowering the dose, and his premium is thirty percent lighter as long as the fills continue. He doesn't know whether that rule is true. He doesn't test it.

Lunch is a chicken breast and half a sleeve of crackers. Someone brought brisket for a retirement, and he takes a slice to be polite and leaves most of it.

After work he drives his mother to Walgreens. Her Medicare pill has been switched again because of the shortage, the third brand since spring, and she is nauseous and furious and pays her fifty dollars anyway. The pharmacist reminds her about the bone scan. She says she'll go in January.

At the ballfield his daughter hits a double. Marcus stands and claps. He notices that he is clapping, and that he means it, more or less.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare is now the single largest insurer of incretin fills.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude: the candidate's own payer mix has commercial at ~12.8M (28%) against Medicare at ~12.2M (27%), so Medicare is not the largest insurer. The prose repeats the claim.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Golden Corral closed ~15% of Florida and Arizona units in 2030.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism: ~3.6M new Medicare oral users among tens of millions of seniors is asserted to explain a double-digit regional closure rate for one chain, with no intermediate chain such as per-meal spend or traffic data.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Year-end health package creates first Medicare Part D obesity benefit, orals only, at $199 net after Novo and Lilly win Section 232 tariff exemptions; CBO scores ~$58B over ten years
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism: the event is dated 2029-07 yet called a 'year-end' package, and the prose says 'last summer' when writing at the end of 2030. Congress also moves from refusing a $41B extension to passing a larger $58B one, with the change attributed to a tariff exemption and no political chain shown.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder, more stratified society, but not a catastrophic one. Medicare coverage helps seniors, while under-65 lower-income adults are left out and the pill shortage disrupts treatment. Quarterly anhedonia questionnaires feed adherence surveillance, and workers tied to a 30% premium game their answers (the Marcus scene). Minors' restrictions sort teen use by income, and the largest unscanned older cohort faces the known hip-fracture risk. The anhedonia label does make the harm nameable (epistemic), which keeps that score moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised: adoption 17.1 (+0.8), the $299→$399 maintenance rise and vial price jump, the Medicare obesity benefit, the March 2030 anhedonia label, the Foundayo switch label, class stratification, minors' restriction and the ad rule, and employer tracks. The approvals (retatrutide, the survodutide CRL, the amycretin filing) obey the envelope's rules. mechanism: The chains are mostly shown: oral API demand, then the shortage, then the allocation. Weaker links are the India rule landing weeks after the TrumpRx price rise, the 'year-end package' dated July (claim 3), and the Golden Corral closures asserted from a thin Medicare effect (claim 2). The anhedonia evidence also arrives fast, via a reanalysis of trials that rarely collected SHAPS data. magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope, and the Medicare arithmetic ($149 × 12 × 3.6M ≈ $6.4B; ~$58B over nine years), the cycling arithmetic and the age-band weights all reconcile. The failures are 'Medicare is the largest insurer' while commercial is larger (claim 1), Medicaid users rising from 3.4M to 3.6M after five states dropped out, and 3.5M versus 3.6M enrollees.
rationale.generativity: The world gives many scenes and characters. The Marcus Bell day shows the adherence app, a mood questionnaire he answers strategically, and his mother's pill switches. Other scenes include Plano DXA percentile swaps, Mesa seniors, families crossing state lines, Unmuted 'off nights', Bread Alone congregations and The Villages' small-plate dining. Daily life is shown with texture rather than only explained.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare is now the single largest insurer of incretin fills.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and reconciliation: the payer mix in population.note puts Medicare at ~12.2M (27%) and commercial at ~12.8M (28%), so Medicare is not the largest insurer.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Her Medicare pill has been switched again because of the shortage, the third brand since spring
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism: the Medicare benefit covers only two oral products (Wegovy pill and Foundayo), so a third brand in one spring is hard to explain, and FDA switching guidance is cited only for allocation-driven substitutions.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Best efficacy is ~27% at 68–80 weeks, uptake is ~0.6M, and supply is limited.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism and magnitude: a ~$899/month cash drug restricted to BMI ≥35 reaching ~0.6M users within about 21 months of approval (Mar 2029 to end-2030) is asserted, and it is not placed in the payer-mix arithmetic.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder, more stratified society. Under-65 low-income adults fall between the price shock, the mail-order squeeze and no coverage; minors are sorted by income across state lines; and adherence-conditioned premiums continue in most states, with anhedonia questionnaires added to the monitoring (the Marcus Bell scene shows him answering carefully).
